title: Apollo 1: Ice in the Dark
tagline: Land on the rim of the Moon's south pole and find water ice.

goal.text: Find signs of water ice inside a permanently shadowed crater near the lunar south pole
goal.why: Water can become drinking water, breathable oxygen and rocket fuel for future crews

inspired_by.name: NASA Artemis III south-pole landing region

facts.text: In 2009 NASA's LCROSS mission crashed a rocket stage into Cabeus crater near the south pole and detected water in the debris plume.
Some craters near the lunar poles never see direct sunlight, so they stay cold enough to trap water ice for billions of years.
NASA's Artemis program plans to land astronauts near the lunar south pole.
Shackleton crater sits almost exactly on the lunar south pole and is about 21 km wide.

candidate_sites.name: Shackleton Rim
candidate_sites.why: Long hours of sunlight on the rim, next to a shadowed crater

candidate_sites.name: Connecting Ridge
candidate_sites.why: High ridge with good views of Earth for radio

candidate_sites.name: de Gerlache Rim
candidate_sites.why: Gentler slopes, a little further from the ice

ship.rationale: The crater floor is in permanent shadow, so the lander needs batteries for about 50 hours of darkness and a drill to reach buried ice.

cruise.story: A burst of solar particles is heading our way. Get the crew behind the water shielding.
Radar shows a field of small debris ahead. Steer through the gaps.
Fuel pressure dropped in line B. Reroute the pipes before the next burn.

tasks.title: Reach the crater rim
tasks.hint: Head toward the edge of the long shadow

tasks.title: Deploy the radio relay
tasks.hint: It needs a clear view of Earth, low on the horizon

tasks.title: Find the ice signal
tasks.hint: Follow the coldest ground: beeps get faster near ice

voice_lines.text: Apollo 1, this is Houston. Your target is the lunar south pole, where sunlight barely reaches and ice may hide in the dark. Build us a ship that can survive the night.
All stations report go. Apollo 1, you are clear for launch.
Apollo 1, pick your landing site carefully. The slopes at the pole are steep.
